title: Family-Owned Turmeric Brings Indian Cooking to Southwest Fort Worth
excerpt: Owner Seshe Sakhamuri, a former principal engineer, has opened her first restaurant in Cityview, serving North Indian staples alongside South Indian, Hyderabadi and Indo-Chinese dishes.
body:
• Turmeric Indian Cuisine, a first restaurant for owner Seshe Sakhamuri and her family, has opened in southwest Fort Worth.
  • The restaurant is at 4608 Bryant Irvin Road, Suite 440, in the Cityview area, south of I-20 — phone (682) 250-5974.
  • The menu spans North Indian staples plus South Indian, Hyderabadi and Indo-Chinese dishes, from butter chicken and biryani to Chicken 65 and naan pizza.
  • Five dishes are marked vegan and 25 gluten-free on the current menu, with spice levels from mild to hot.

Southwest Fort Worth has a new family-owned Indian restaurant. Turmeric Indian Cuisine opened on Sunday south of Interstate 20 off Bryant Irvin Road, according to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram, giving the Hulen and Cityview neighbourhoods an Indian option in an area dominated by chain restaurants. It is the first restaurant for owner Seshe Sakhamuri and her family.

An engineer who followed her cooking

Sakhamuri made the move into restaurants after years working as a principal engineer, the Star-Telegram reported, describing the opening as a leap of faith to follow her passion for cooking. That career-change story is familiar across the diaspora — a professional leaves a technical job to cook the food she grew up with — but it is the menu, published in full on the restaurant's official site, that shows how the family intends to compete.

What is on the menu

Turmeric describes its cooking as Indian, South Indian, Hyderabadi and Indo-Chinese, at a mid-range price point. The entry points are deliberately familiar: butter chicken in a tomato, butter and cream gravy, and chicken tikka masala with tandoor-charred chicken, both served with rice. Beyond those, the kitchen lists house special biryani, Chicken 65 finished with curry leaves, Chettinad dishes built on roasted coconut and black pepper, and goat sukka cooked with Mangalorean spices.

Two items are aimed squarely at first-timers and families: a naan pizza, built on a tandoori naan base with spiced tomato sauce, cheese and red onion, with paneer or chicken as add-ons, and a naan taco. The restaurant also offers catering for office lunches, parties and community events, built around curries, biryani and naan.

Options for restricted diets

The menu labelling is unusually explicit for a new independent restaurant. Five dishes are marked vegan as written, including aloo gobi, okra fry, chana masala and mixed vegetable Chettinad, and 25 dishes are marked gluten-free, including all four biryanis and many curries. The restaurant notes that cross-contact cannot be guaranteed because the kitchen also handles wheat. Spice can be ordered mild, medium or hot, with the korma and butter chicken recommended as the gentlest starting points.

Visiting Turmeric

Turmeric Indian Cuisine is at 4608 Bryant Irvin Road, Suite 440, Fort Worth, TX 76132, in the Cityview area, and can be reached at (682) 250-5974. For Indian families in southwest Fort Worth — until now better served by the Indian restaurants of Irving, Plano and Frisco — it is a local option for a weeknight thali-style dinner or a Diwali-season family meal without the cross-metro drive. First-time visitors unsure where to start can follow the restaurant's own advice: a butter chicken or tikka masala, rice included, plus a garlic naan.
